name: Kazi Istiak Toriqe
role: Software R&D, Samsung Research Bangladesh | Prospective PhD Applicant, Fall 2027
headline: Hello, I’m Kazi Istiak Toriqe.
intro: Thank you for visiting my little corner of the internet. Looking back at my years at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, some of my favorite moments were the ones spent figuring out why something did not work: an unexpected page fault, a scheduler behaving strangely, or a program that refused to produce the result I expected. Those experiences gradually turned curiosity into a lasting affection for building things and understanding them from the inside.
questions: How can lightweight execution models support more concurrent work with less scheduling overhead?
How can replication and recovery protocols provide strong guarantees without unnecessary coordination?
How can the data path of a networked system minimize copies, blocking and wasted resources?

research.title: Patient Similarity Detection via Contrastive Learning
research.description: Undergraduate thesis on patient similarity from Stanford Wearable PPG and PTB Diagnostic ECG signals. Adapted ResNeXt and EfficientNet to 1D time series, investigated contrastive learning and similarity aggregation, and evaluated results against baselines. Manuscript will be submitted to a Q1 journal.

projects.title: Samsung Health Monitor · Sleep Apnea
projects.text: Implemented asynchronous Wear OS–Android message protocols; contributed to sensor sessions, recovery after boot/permission changes, health-data backup/restore, power-aware sensor activity and improved connection handling in collaboration with Samsung teams in America and Korea.
bullets: Designed asynchronous message protocols between Wear OS and Android for Samsung Health Monitor’s Sleep Apnea feature, collaborating with Samsung Research America.
Worked on sensor collection, session management, and recovery after device reboot or permission changes.
Contributed to health-data backup, restore, and synchronization interfaces with Samsung Health SDK, collaborating with Samsung Korea.
Reduced unnecessary sensor activity and polling; refactored connection handling with an approximately 2× connection-establishment improvement (as measured internally).

projects.title: FlashShare · Fault-Tolerant LAN File Sharing
projects.text: Designed a high-throughput peer-to-peer file transfer system supporting fanout and relay topologies. Separated user-space coordination from the data path, investigated low-copy Linux mechanisms, and designed progress-aware relay recovery. Further data-path work is ongoing.
bullets: Designed a high-throughput peer-to-peer system for large LAN file transfers with fanout and relay topologies.
Separated user-space control protocols from the bulk data path; implemented direct transfers with Linux sendfile().
Exploring splice()/tee() for low-copy relay forwarding and designing progress-aware recovery after relay failures.

projects.title: disKeyV
projects.subtitle: Logless replication and recovery
projects.description: An ongoing experimental logless distributed key–value store built around segment-based replication and recovery. It uses TCP communication, heartbeat-based failure detection and leader transitions, with crash recovery and safe-read handling. Further work considers software-emulated RDMA-style transport and recovery correctness.

projects.title: User-Level Thread Library
projects.subtitle: Lightweight execution on Linux
projects.description: Built a Linux user-level threading library from scratch with cooperative and preemptive scheduling, context switching, thread lifecycle management, and sleep/wake-up mechanisms.

projects.title: Kernel Threads on xv6
projects.subtitle: Kernel concurrency mechanisms
projects.description: Extended the xv6 kernel with threads sharing a process address space. Worked with thread creation, kernel scheduling behavior, and synchronization involving locks and semaphores, including challenges caused by sharing process resources across concurrent execution.

projects.title: Paging and Swap in xv6
projects.subtitle: Virtual memory implementation
projects.description: Implemented on-demand paging and swap-space support in xv6, including page-fault trap handling, bookkeeping for resident and swapped pages, an LRU-style eviction policy, and moving evicted pages to and from secondary storage.

projects.description: Implemented a subset of a C compiler with Flex/Bison bottom-up parsing, scoped symbol tables, semantic processing, parse-tree construction, and on-the-fly intermediate code generation.

intro2: After graduating from BUET, I joined Samsung Research Bangladesh, where I have continued to learn from the practical challenges of building dependable software with others. Outside work, I still enjoy experimenting with ideas, revisiting old projects, and writing about mathematics. I am preparing to apply for PhD programs for Fall 2027, with the goal of pursuing original research in computer systems. This website collects some of the work and interests that have brought me here.
